title: Real player input contract, version 1
description: A versioned contract for real player data entering the championship-equity engine. It deliberately carries ONLY quantities whose meaning is proven end to end (see docs/PLAYER_DATA_LINEAGE.md). Anything whose meaning is unresolved is either absent or must be declared in open_questions. It preserves every raw source field verbatim so that a mapping judgement can be revisited without a re-import. This schema does not describe a dataset that exists; it describes the shape one must take to be trusted.

schema_version.description: Bump when the MEANING of any field changes, not only its shape. A source column silently redefined upstream is the failure mode this exists to catch.

league_config_id.description: Which league's scoring and roster rules this was built for. PLAYER_DATA_INVENTORY.md Q6: the existing player model is configured for a 10-team league with no superflex while this engine specifies 12 teams with one, so this must be explicit.

sources.description: One entry per input file, identified by content hash rather than filename. PLAYER_DATA_INVENTORY.md 1.1 records a case where the later-sounding filename held the older data.

retrieved_at.description: Null is permitted and meaningful: at least one real source carries no update timestamp and cannot be dated.

role.description: Market sources may appear here for traceability but must never populate a performance field.

scoring_support.description: Which of this league's scoring categories the source can actually compute. A missing category is NOT zero.

unsupported_categories.description: Categories in this league's rules with no source column. Recorded so that a total is never mistaken for complete. Known gaps: pass_2pt, rush_2pt, rec_2pt, special_teams_td.

treated_as.description: Only 'absent' is legal. Silently substituting zero is the error this field exists to prevent.

uncalibrated_parameters.description: Engine parameters this input cannot supply, carried so a run built on it can always say which parts of its answer rest on data. See docs/PLAYER_MAPPING_GAPS.md section 4.

open_questions.description: Unresolved semantic questions that affect the values below. A consumer may refuse to run while any blocking question is open.

player_key.description: Stable join key, normalised from the name. Also the seed for the engine's crn_key.

nfl_team.description: Null where the identity join did not match. Null means unknown, never a default team.

bye_week.description: Null where absent. Proven meaning. Must not be coerced to 0.

stat_line.description: Season-long component projections. Proven to be the vendor's component stats; NOT proven to be means rather than medians (open question Q4), and the projection window is unstated (Q1).

stat_line_horizon.description: Everything needed to turn the stat line into a per-week mean. Required alongside stat_line precisely because the source does not state it.

games_assumed.description: Games the season total is spread over. Null means unresolved; a consumer must refuse rather than assume 16 or 17.

conditional_on_playing.description: True if the projection describes weeks the player actually plays. Null means unresolved (Q3) -- applying an availability haircut on top would double-count.

central_tendency.description: 'unknown' is the honest value for the current source and must be preserved rather than assumed to be 'mean'.

availability.description: Vendor availability signals. The EXTRACTION is proven; the vendor's DEFINITIONS are not (Q5), which is why definition strings are required alongside the numbers.

injury_prob_definition.description: The vendor's own definition of the event. Null means unknown; a consumer must not convert it to a weekly hazard without one.

games_in_horizon.description: Denominator proj_games_missed is measured against. The existing model uses 16 in one place and 17 in another; a contract must pick one.

cohort_dispersion.description: Dispersion from a fitted cohort statistic, not a per-player measurement. Both fields have fully proven definitions (docs/PLAYER_DATA_LINEAGE.md section 3).

weekly_cv.description: Positional coefficient of variation: mean over qualifying player-seasons of std(weekly half-PPR)/mean(weekly half-PPR), computed over APPEARED weeks with ddof=0. A cohort average applied to an individual.

weekly_cv_is_total_dispersion.description: Asserts the caller knows this is TOTAL weekly dispersion, not the unforecastable part. The engine splits week_sd from weekly_state_sd; this figure does not carry that split.

weekly_miss_rate.description: P(does not appear in week w+1 | contributed in week w), byes excluded. Counts ANY non-appearance -- benching, rest and trade included -- so it is an availability hazard, not an injury hazard.

fit_provenance.description: Seasons, cohort and sample size the fit came from.

expert_labels.description: Ordinal expert labels. Recorded for traceability ONLY. They are not distributional quantities and no mapping from them to a standard deviation exists; see docs/PLAYER_MAPPING_GAPS.md section 3.

may_derive_dispersion.description: Pinned false. The raw upside tag correlates +0.53 with projected points; it substantially restates player quality, not variance.

raw_fields.description: Every source field verbatim, under its ORIGINAL column name, before any mapping. Required, and required to be non-empty: every mapping decision above is a judgement that will be revisited, and discarding the inputs turns a re-derivation into a re-import.

stat_line.description: Component stats. Every field is optional and null-permitting: a null means NOT PROJECTED, which is not the same as zero. The existing source leaves Rush TDs blank on 77.6% of rows and Rec TDs on 52.1%.

fumbles.description: The source column is named 'Fumbles'. Whether it means fumbles LOST -- which is what this league scores -- is open question Q2.

fumbles_are_lost_fumbles.description: Null means unresolved. A consumer must not apply the -2 lost-fumble rule while this is null.
